name: MessageWatch
author: Nyanako
short: Flag scam and hostile messages to moderators with a System One model.
description: Watches explicitly enabled channels, judges short rolling windows of messages with TypeSafe Jev, and reports scam attempts and hostile exchanges to a moderator channel. It never deletes, edits, reacts to, or punishes anything.
install_msg: Load with `[p]load messagewatch`, store the key with `[p]watch key`, set a report channel, then enable each watched channel one at a time with `[p]watch enable`. Read the displayed disclosure first: enabled channels send message text off Discord continuously, with nobody triggering it.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores per-guild settings, the report channel ID, and the set of channel IDs a guild manager has explicitly enabled. It does not store message content, model responses, or any judgement. It stores per-guild counts of how moderators marked reports, as totals only. The API key is stored only by Red's shared API token system. In an enabled channel, the text of each recent human message, its position in the window, a per-run pseudonymous author label, and the name of the channel are sent to TypeSafe for judgement. Where a guild manager has configured rules for a channel, those rules and the channel's purpose note are sent with every request as well; both are written by a moderator, not by members. The configured rules, the purpose note, the report-route channel ID set by [p]watch route, the list of report buttons, the role ID the role button adds, and a per-channel rule-violation threshold set by [p]watch rule threshold, and whether image reading is enabled are stored per channel. Discord user IDs, display names, and avatars are never sent: authors are replaced with labels such as u1 and u2 that are generated per request and never persisted. Embeds and links are not fetched or resolved. Where a guild manager has enabled image reading for a channel, image attachments in that channel are downloaded, downscaled and re-encoded (which discards EXIF, including any GPS tags), then sent to a separate vision provider that is asked only to transcribe the characters in them; that transcription is shown in the report so a moderator can check it against the image. Image reading is off unless it is turned on for a channel individually. TypeSafe states it does not train on customer input; its retention terms and the accuracy of its judgements are unverified by this cog. A channel sends nothing until a guild manager enables it individually, and disabling it stops the sending immediately. Reports name the channel, the flagged message and its author so a moderator can act. The bot never acts on its own: a report can carry buttons, and only a moderator holding the matching Discord permission can press one. Deleting a message, timing a member out and adding a role happen only on such a press, and each is recorded in the modlog under that moderator's name.
